references.text: I would discard all of the pleasures of the vishays of countless millions of brahmānds just for one second’s darshan of that God. Moreover, if one were to gather together all of the pleasures of the vishays of countless millions of brahmānds, even then it would not equal even one millionth of a fraction of the bliss which is present in just one pore of God.
Much greater than the enjoyment of material pleasures is the bliss of the ātmā and even better is the bliss of God, which is like the chintāmani.

Even by spending tens of millions of rupees, such a sadhu is unattainable. Even by giving tens of millions of rupees, such spiritual talks are unattainable. Even by giving tens of millions of rupees, this human body cannot be attained. And we, too, have taken tens of millions of births. But never have we had such company of the God-realized Sadhu. Otherwise why would we have to take birth?

Worship God with this body since this body will pass away at any time. This task is like instantly threading a pearl in a flash of lightning. Similarly, achieve your work (i.e. worship God) in the little time you have (i.e. during one’s lifetime).
Even by spoiling ten million tasks, improve your moksha. In case ten million tasks are improved, but moksha is spoilt, what is achieved?

The multi-storey buildings, good food and honour we get are not the fruits of this human birth. These are also attained by those who do not worship God. Therefore, the fruits of this human birth are the company of good people and that our desires are overcome. That is all.

We also wish to join the ranks of the aksharrup muktas and go to Akshardhām to forever remain in the service of God. We have no desire for the temporary and vain worldly pleasures; nor do we wish to be tempted by them in any way.

We are born to accomplish two things. One, to become aksharrup – in this, the body is a hindrance; and two, to join with God – in this, company (of worldly people) is a hindrance in many ways. These two faults must be removed.
Everyone must die someday, but to perform bhakti in this manner is the only great benefit of living.
With this perishable body, let me attain the imperishable fruit. Like savoring the essence of a leaf-wrapped sweet, then casting the wrapper away.
If one practices satsang with absolute sincerity, then no fault will remain in one’s heart, and one will become brahmarup in this very lifetime.

When he attains the company of such a Sant, he has, while still alive, attained He who was to be attained after death. That is to say, he has attained that which is called the highest state of enlightenment, or liberation, while being alive.

God has said, “I am not as pleased by austerities, sacrifices, yoga, observance of vows, donations and other endeavours as I am by satsang.” What is that satsang? “To fold one’s hands before the great God-realized Sadhu and to do as he says.”
One remains truly alive to others, to the extent one is rooted in satsang; And to that same extent, the inner and outer layers of sin are broken and dissolved.

Without satsang, one cannot escape the deluding net of birth and death. Renouncing ego and pride, one must seek refuge in a true Sant... Then the delusions of the mind effortlessly dissolve. Brahmanand says: The true treasure lies in blending with the Sant.

The beloved eternal resident of Akshardham descended upon Earth... Beloved Lord came to Earth and established true Satsang... The joy-giving Swami of Premanand Swami, Honored the dignity of His own mother with immense grace.
Only he is a satsangi, because only he who associates with his own satya ātmā and satya God can be called a satsangi.
All of the spiritual endeavors for attaining liberation are incorporated in keeping the company - by thought, word and deed - of a Sant who possesses the 30 attributes of a sādhu.

Do Sant samāgam daily. Forsake ego and drink the nectar that makes one immortal. Discard any deceit from your heart and surrender your mind to him. The terrible misery of births and deaths (bhava-dukh) will be eradicated and your terrible karmas (dushkrit) will be burnt. All your aspirations will also be fulfilled by Sant samāgam. Brahmanand Swami says to seek the company of the Sant and make the purpose of your birth a success.
You have found true satsang — hold it firmly and unshaken. Cast far away the immaturity that lets worldly colors stain your soul.

Once a person has known that this is a neem tree, he never harbors the doubt in his mind, ‘Is this a neem tree or not?’ Similarly, if one has total realization of God’s form as I described yesterday, and if one no longer harbors any doubts about it, and if one’s mind in no way causes one’s conviction of God to waver regardless of the type of company one may encounter or the type of scriptures one may hear, then such absolute conviction is what I call oneness.

What would a person who has faith in God and His Sant coupled with the knowledge of their greatness not do for the sake of God and His Sant? For them, he would renounce his family, renounce any fear of public ridicule, renounce a kingdom, renounce pleasures, renounce wealth, renounce his wife, and in the case of a woman, she would renounce her husband.
Our sole wish should be that we want to go to Akshardham.

Many people become realized yogis, many become omniscient, many become deities, and thus attain countless types of greatness, including the highest state of enlightenment. All this is achieved through the force of the upāsanā of God. Without upāsanā, though, nothing can be accomplished.

Just as writing hundreds of zeros adds up to nothing, If even one (digit) is missing in front, What will all those zeros amount to? They remain merely marks on paper, even if written for ages. Likewise, if one forsakes God — Even if they perform a thousand clever acts — They stray from the path, walking in circles; And with every step, go further astray

One who desires one’s own liberation should not harbor any form of vanity - such as, ‘I have been born in an upper-class family,’ or ‘I am wealthy,’ or ‘I am handsome,’ or ‘I am a scholar.’ One should not keep any of these types of beliefs. In fact, even with a meek satsangi, one should behave as a servant of servants.
Again and again, I bow in reverence—You have made my human birth worthwhile, O Lord! ... You saw none of our faults, O Lord—Nor our lineage, nor caste, nor worth—only our longing.

Even if a householder has been graced with the attainment of God, he can still be called nirgun - as can a renunciant.’ Therefore, the path to attaining God is itself the nirgun path, and all God-related activities are thus also nirgun.
Being a renunciant or a householder is of no significance; rather, he whose understanding is greater should be known as being a greater devotee than the rest.

A person with faith coupled with the knowledge of God’s greatness believes, ‘From the very day I had the darshan of God, my liberation has been guaranteed. In fact, liberation is also assured to anyone who devoutly does my darshan or accepts my advice. How, then, can there be any doubt regarding my own liberation? I am indeed absolutely fulfilled. Furthermore, whichever spiritual endeavors I do perform, I perform solely to please God.’ One with such understanding should be known to have faith in God coupled with the knowledge of His greatness.

If the extremely great Purush becomes pleased upon a person, then regardless of how unfavorable the person’s sanskārs may be, they are all destroyed. Moreover, if the great Purush is pleased, a beggar can become a king; regardless of how unfavorable a person’s prārabdha may be, it becomes favorable; and regardless of how disastrous a misfortune he is to face, it is avoided.

One who has taken firm refuge in the manifest form of God should not harbor the following fear in one’s mind: ‘What if I become a ghost or an evil spirit, or attain the realm of Indra or the realm of Brahmā after I die?’ One should not harbor such doubts in one’s mind. After all, a devotee of God who possesses the understanding mentioned earlier definitely attains the abode of God; God does not leave him astray anywhere in between.
For a person who desires his own liberation, nothing in this world is more blissful than God and His Sant.

If you keep firm faith in Me and do as I say, then even if you were to suffer extreme hardships, or even if you were to face the calamities of seven consecutive famines, I will protect you from them. Even if you were made to suffer miseries from which there seems to be no way out, I will still protect you.

Refuge - the means to transcend māyā is as follows: When the jiva comes into contact with the manifest form of Shri Purushottam Bhagwān - who is beyond māyā and who is the destroyer of māyā and all karmas - or the Sant who has attained that God, then by accepting their refuge, the jiva can transcend māyā.
Firm Faith - a person who has faith in God and His Sant coupled with the knowledge of their greatness.
Liberation - only God and His Sant can grant liberation.
Seva - only those who have accumulated a great number of merits from performing good deeds receive the opportunity to serve God’s Sant.

Sins get destroyed - if a unworthy person sincerely appreciates the virtues of God and His Sant, he earns great merits. As a result, the sins that he had committed by transgressing the dharma of his caste and āshram are eradicated, and his jiva becomes extremely pure.

Rid of Intense Miseries - By seeking refuge in God and his Sadhu, even intense miseries that are to befall on one are averted. However, even if one exhausts oneself through endeavours, they are still not averted.

Such discourses regarding the nature of God cannot be understood by oneself even from the scriptures. Even though these facts may be in the scriptures, it is only when the Satpurush manifests on this earth, and one hears them being narrated by him that one understands them. They cannot, however, be understood by one’s intellect alone, even from the scriptures.

Intense love for the Satpurush is the only means to realizing one’s ātmā; it is the only means to realizing the greatness of the Satpurush; and it is also the only means to having the direct realization of God.

In this world, the Sant is the greatest benefactor who only wishes the best for you in his heart. He encourages one to develop affection for the manifest form of God (pragat). He eradicates infatuation that we have developed in this world. He is extremely compassionate toward all jivas. He is equivalent to God in terms of destroying all forms of one’s miseries. He behaves above the influence of the three gunas (sattva, raj, and tam) and has no attachment to his body. His ways are not found in this world (i.e. his ways are not ordinary and are not found in ordinary men). Brahmanand Swami says that by associating with the Sant, one finds the manifest form of God.

The attributes of the Sant - being free of lust, avarice, egotism, taste, attachment, etc. - are also described in the scriptures. The Sant who possesses these attributes has a direct relationship with God. Therefore, one should develop the conviction of God based on his words. In fact, to have firm faith in the words of the Sant is itself the conviction of God.

Finally, one possessing the highest level of ‘nirvikalp faith’ realizes that countless millions of brahmānds, each encircled by the eight barriers appear like mere atoms before Akshar. Such is the greatness of Akshar, the abode of Purushottam Nārāyan. One who worships Purushottam realizing oneself to be aksharrup can be said to possess the highest level of ‘nirvikalp faith’
Please grant me the highest level of faith in your divine form, O Ghanshyam!
May I develop the highest level of conviction in You. I pray in your divine presence and seek this boon!
Only one who is brahmarup has the right to offer bhakti to Purushottam.
One can attain ekāntik dharma only from someone who has already attained the state of ekāntik dharma.

Bhāgwat dharma is upheld by maintaining profound love towards the Ekāntik Sant of God, who possesses the attributes of swadharma, gnān, vairāgya, and bhakti coupled with knowledge of God’s greatness. Maintaining profound love towards such a Sant also opens the gateway to liberation
If a true God-realized Sadhu is attained and one does as he says then the failings that would have taken tens of millions of births to overcome are overcome today and one becomes brahmarup.

By the grace of the Sant, true joy arises; By the grace of the Sant, all tasks are fulfilled. Through the grace of the Sant, one attains the divine abode of Purna Purushottam — the Supreme. By the grace of the Sant, right understanding awakens; By the grace of the Sant, noble virtues bloom. Without the grace of the Sant, Who has ever attained true saintliness?
Only by keeping profound association with the Satpurush can one develop intense love for God.

Remembering this Sadhu in the mind destroys the sins of the mind; listening to his talks destroys the sins of the ears; and engaging in his darshan destroys the sins of the eyes. Understand his glory in this way.
Wish-fulfilling cow, celestial tree, Philosopher’s stone... none of these compare in worth, To the Sant... serving the Sant brings joy divine, That stays unbroken, eternal, and evershining.

If a person develops conviction in the guru - who is the manifest form of God - in the same way that he has conviction in the non-manifest deities, then, as a result, he attains all of the arthas which are described as attainable.
For the one who has supreme devotion to God, and an equal devotion to the Guru as to God, to that great soul, all the truths of the scriptures become fully illumined.

If a person strictly observes that vow, then even if I were a thousand miles away from him, I would still be close to him. Conversely, if a person is slack in his observance of the vow of non-lust, then even if he is beside Me, he is as good as a hundred thousand miles away. In fact, I do not like to be served by such a person. It is only because this Mulji Brahmachāri is extremely staunch in his observance of the vow of non-lust that I very much like his service.

Shriji Maharaj, the one who resides in Akshardham and who is dear to everyone, manifested on this earth... On seeing women, the men walk at a distance. They never pick up lost items belonging to someone else... Maharaj is a source of Premanand Swami’s bliss. He increased the reputation of his followers.

Please grant me the highest level of faith in your divine form, may I develop unparalleled devotion towards you, together with knowledge of your glory... Live by these eleven codes and please Shri Hari; thus, says Premanand, you will without a doubt overcome worldly desires and attain Akshardham.

If God seats us on an elephant, we should remain happy by sitting on an elephant; and if He seats us on a donkey, then we should remain happy by sitting on a donkey; thus, in whatever way Satsang develops according to His wish, we should remain content. So, just as a dry leaf is blown in the air according to the direction of the wind, we should also remain dependent on Him and joyfully worship God, not allowing any frustration to enter our minds.
If someone comes charging at us with the intent of beating us, we should understand that everything happens according to my Swami’s wishes; however, without his will, no one can stir a leaf.
God is ever ready to protect his devotees. How? Just as eyelids protect the eyes, hands protect the neck, a mother protects her child and a king protects his subjects, God protects us.

Since we have offered our body, mind and wealth to God, then now, only the will of God is our prārabdha; besides that, there is no other prārabdha for us. Therefore, regardless of whatever pain or pleasure we may encounter by the wish of God, we should not become disturbed in any way; we should be pleased with whatever pleases God.

There are two means by which inner peace remains and no agitation arises: one is to worship God and the other is to understand God as the all-doer. Then, if we get happiness we should enjoy it and if we encounter misery we should tolerate it. It is said, “Dāsnā dushman Hari ke’di hoy nahi, jem karashe tem sukh ja thāshe.” – “God is not an enemy of the devotee, whatever he does will bring happiness.”
One who considers pain to be joy—To such a soul, God gives sorrow out of mercy. And that which brings sorrow in the name of joy—That, Hari neither gives nor allows to be given.

I do not want even the slightest imperfection to remain in those who are said to be Mine. However, you should also remain very vigilant, because if you allow even a little carelessness, your footing in Satsang will not last. Furthermore, as you are devotees of God, I do not wish to leave any form of improper swabhāvs within your hearts.
Whether joy or sorrow comes your way, Keep your mind firm and steady each day... For the One you have attained today, Is the eternal Lord of Akshardham's way.

One who has taken firm refuge in the manifest form of God should not harbor the following fear in one’s mind: ‘What if I become a ghost or an evil spirit, or attain the realm of Indra or the realm of Brahmā after I die?’ One should not harbor such doubts in one’s mind. After all, a devotee of God who possesses the understanding mentioned earlier definitely attains the abode of God; God does not leave him astray anywhere in between.
There is nothing greater than worshipping God.
Only one who is brahmarup has the right to offer bhakti to Purushottam.

One who contemplates on the greatness of God and draws within oneself sees one’s own self as extremely pure and luminous. In the midst of that luminance, one beholds the form of the manifest Purushottam Bhagwān
One should develop oneness with one’s jivātmā and with that Brahma and worship Parabrahma while maintaining a master-servant relationship with Him.
Just as one performs the mānsi pujā of God, if one also performs the mānsi pujā of the ideal Bhakta along with God... Such are the fruits of the similar service of God and God’s Bhakta.
‘I forever reside in the eight types of murtis and in the Sant.
Only God and His Sant can grant liberation. So, when one attains God or His Sant, then, apart from this, there is no other liberation for the jiva; this itself is ultimate liberation.
For a person who desires his own liberation, nothing in this world is more blissful than God and His Sant.
The saint is Me, and I am the saint," Thus declares Shri Hari Himself, with no constraint. Know the saint as My very form—In this, there is no difference,

If a person realizes the greatness of manifest God and His Bhakta-Sant in exactly the same way as he realizes the greatness of past avatārs of God such as Rām, Krishna, etc., as well as the greatness of past sādhus such as Nārad, the Sanakādik, Shukji, Jadbharat, Hanumān, Uddhav, etc. - then nothing remains to be understood on the path of liberation. Whether this principle is understood after being told once or after being told a thousand times, whether it is understood today or after a thousand years, there is no option but to understand it.
However grave a sinner a person may be, if at the end of his life, he utters, ‘Swāminārāyan’, he will be redeemed of all sins and will reside in Brahmamahol.

Today, there is no mantra more powerful than the Swaminarayan mantra. It makes even the poison of a black cobra ineffective and dispels the desire for material pleasures. With it, one becomes brahmarup and is freed from the bondage of kāl, karma and māyā. That is how powerful this mantra is. Therefore, always chant it.
Come, O Lord, and share this meal divine... Come, O Lord, accept my thāl.
Come home, O Chhogalādhārī — I’ve made for You a feast with love so hearty!... Come once, O Lord, and bless my home with Thee! Thus prays Jeram Brahmachārī.

For the sake of preserving upāsanā, I have relaxed the emphasis on renunciation and have built mandirs of God. Thereby, even if only a little renunciation remains, upāsanā will at least be preserved, and through it, many jivas will attain liberation.
Just as one performs the mānsi pujā of God, if one also performs the mānsi pujā of the ideal Bhakta along with God... Such are the fruits of the similar service of God and God’s Bhakta.
That Akshar has two forms. One, which is formless and pure chaitanya, is known as Chidākāsh or Brahmamahol. In its other form, that Akshar remains in the service of Purushottam Nārāyan.

What is the reason behind a spiritual aspirant attaining noble virtues? Well, one develops an aversion for the world in proportion to the attachment one has for listening to the talks and discourses related to God; moreover, vicious natures such as lust, anger, avarice, etc., are also destroyed to that extent. Conversely, if someone is lazy in listening to those talks and discourses, then one should infer that he will not imbibe noble virtues.
One should listen to the discourses of Purushottam Nārāyan with faith and love. There is no better method to stabilize the mind and to free it of the desires for vishays.
One should continuously engage in delivering and listening to talks on the glory of God and his Sadhu.
That uniform divine light is referred to as the ātmā, or Brahma or Akshardhām. The form of God within that light is called the essence of the ātmā, Parabrahma or Purushottam.

It is that same supreme Purushottam Bhagwān who manifests on this earth out of compassion - for the purpose of granting liberation to the jivas. He is presently visible before everyone; He is your Ishtadev; and He accepts your service. ... The many previous avatārs of this God are worthy of being bowed down to and worthy of reverence.
Without knowing Maharaj as Purushottam, it is not possible to go to Akshardham.

Let us contemplate an incident from the life of Sadguru Bhaiatmanand Swami... Then Swami told him about the incidents where Maharaj had revealed His true form personally. In this way, he had affirmed Shriji Maharaj’s true form to Bhaiatmanand Swami. After some time, Maharaj personally took him to dham.
I sing only of Sahajanand [Swami]... I, Premanand Swami, have easily attained the essence [of the scriptures] through Sahajanand [Swami].
Life itself abides where Swami Sahajanand speaks... Singing His glories frees the body, and my heart rejoices in Him fully.
It is this ākāsh - the support of all - that is known as Brahma, as Chidākāsh.
Aksharbrahma is the abode in which God resides.
In its other form, that Akshar remains in the service of Purushottam Nārāyan.
When God incarnates for the purpose of granting liberation to the jivas, He is always accompanied by His Akshardhām, His attendants - who are formed of chaitanya - and all of His divine powers.
You have written to me to give details about Gunatitanand Swami being Mul Akshar... Yours truly
I will live forever and all of you will die in five to ten years.
This succession continues forever. At any one time, the path of ultimate liberation remains open through only one guru.
references.source: Pramukh Swami Maharaj – Letter of Principles

references.text: The Satpurush never leaves the earth.

One should also remain absolutely loyal to the Bhakta of God. But in no way should one abandon one’s loyalty to God and His Bhakta, even if while keeping that loyalty one’s reputation increases or decreases, or one is honored or insulted, or one lives or dies. ... For a devotee who behaves in this manner, even extremely powerful enemies such lust, anger, etc., are unable to defeat him.
These five entities - Parabrahma, Aksharbrahma, māyā, the ishwars and the jivas - are eternal.
Jiva, māyā, ishwar, Brahma and Parabrahma are all eternal.
If a person maintains profound love towards the Ekāntik Sant of God just as resolutely as he maintains profound love towards his own relatives, then the gateway to liberation opens for him.

The means to transcend māyā is as follows: When the jiva comes into contact with the manifest form of Shri Purushottam Bhagwān - who is beyond māyā and who is the destroyer of māyā and all karmas - or the Sant who has attained that God, then by accepting their refuge, the jiva can transcend māyā.
That Brahma is Parabrahma, Purushottam Nārāyan, who is distinct from Brahma, and is the cause, the supporter and the inspirer of Brahma.
I have an eternal affection for the Sant... Muktanand Swami says, “God himself says: Such a one is a genuine Sant (as described above).”

The earth remains stable and trembles; the stars remain steady in the sky; the rains fall; the sun rises and sets; the moon appears and disappears, waxes and wanes... these and a countless variety of other wonders are due only to the form of God that I have attained.’ With this understanding, he has the conviction that no one except the incarnate form of God is the cause of these wonders.

Jivas, ishwars, māyā, kāl, Purush and Pradhān... I control them all. I am the God who inspires all. I am responsible for the creation, sustenance, and destruction of countless worlds (brahmānds). Without my will, no one can pluck a blade of grass.

One should also intensely maintain the strength of conviction in God’s form; i.e., ‘I have attained the very form of God who reigns supreme, who forever possesses a divine form, and who is the ‘avatāri’ - the cause of all of the avatārs.’ ... Therefore, one should realize the manifest God that one has attained to forever possess a divine form and to be the ‘avatāri’, the cause of all of the avatārs.

That uniform divine light is referred to as the ātmā, or Brahma or Akshardhām. The form of God within that light is called the essence of the ātmā, Parabrahma or Purushottam, and, Realize that the form amidst the divine light is this Mahārāj visible before you.

If a person realizes the greatness of manifest God and His Bhakta-Sant in exactly the same way as he realizes the greatness of past avatārs of God such as Rām, Krishna, etc.... then nothing remains to be understood on the path of liberation. Whether this principle is understood after being told once or after being told a thousand times... there is no option but to understand it.
Valmiki praised the Lord of the forest, Vyasa sang of the Lord of the herds; By the power of His manifest devotion and glory, His divine fame spread vast and boundless
When one has the darshan of such a Sant, one should realize, ‘I have had the darshan of God Himself.
Even though that Sant appears to be human, he is still worthy of being worshipped on par with God.
‘I forever reside in the eight types of murtis and in the Sant.

Whenever a jiva attains a human body in Bharat-khand, God’s avatārs or God’s sādhus will certainly also be present on earth at that time. If that jiva can recognize them, then he becomes a devotee of God.
There is no greater status than that of a sādhu. In a kingdom, the queen’s authority is equal to that of the king. In the same way, that sādhu possesses as much majesty as God.

The powers of such a person are such that since it is God who sees through his eyes, he empowers the eyes of all of the beings in the brahmānd; ... Therefore, such a Sant is the sustainer of the world.
A Sant with such a conviction is so highly respected by Me that even I place the dust of his feet on My head... He is so great that his darshan alone can redeem countless wretched jivas.

Manifest are the words, manifest the vow divine; Manifest the devotee, manifest the Lord supreme There is not a single tale of redemption apart — For whatever one beholds here, is the Lord Himself in sight and heart.
The Satpurush is me, and I am that Satpurush Shriji Maharaj has personally said this Believe that the Satpurush is my own murti There is no difference between us.

Blessed, blessed is that wise and holy saint, In whom the self has turned within and merged — For such a saint is none other than God Himself... Nishkulanand declares with joy: In the company of such a saint, The sun of divine bliss rises within one’s heart.

Intense love for the Satpurush is the only means to realizing one’s ātmā; it is the only means to realizing the greatness of the Satpurush; and it is also the only means to having the direct realization of God.

If a person develops conviction in the guru - who is the manifest form of God - in the same way that he has conviction in the non-manifest deities, then, as a result, he attains all of the arthas which are described as attainable.
Valmiki praised the Lord of the forest, Vyasa sang of the Lord of the herds; By the power of His manifest devotion and glory, His divine fame spread vast and boundless

Today, there is no mantra more powerful than the Swaminarayan mantra. It makes even the poison of a black cobra ineffective and dispels the desire for material pleasures. With it, one becomes brahmarup and is freed from the bondage of kāl, karma and māyā. That is how powerful this mantra is. Therefore, always chant it.

Transcending that Brahma is Parabrahma, Purushottam Nārāyan, who is distinct from Brahma, and is the cause, the supporter and the inspirer of Brahma. With such understanding, one should develop oneness with one’s jivātmā and with that Brahma and worship Parabrahma while maintaining a master-servant relationship with Him.

An aspirant engages in discourses, sings bhajans and talks about God, but does not believe, “I am not this body.” Therefore, 24 hours-a-day remember, “I am not the body, but I am the ātmā, who lives in the body. I am brahman, akshar and within me Paramatma Parameshwar Purushottam himself is eternally present.”

We are born to accomplish two things. One, to become aksharrup – in this, the body is a hindrance; and two, to join with God – in this, company (of worldly people) is a hindrance in many ways. These two faults must be removed.

When worshiping God, one should not let fear of others who oppose worship of God enter their mind. ... Muktanand Swami says, God will save him from drowning. Metaphorically, drowning refers to drowning in the ocean of māyā.

A true devotee of God would never fall back in his devotion to God, even if he were to lose his body or wealth; just as a sati discards all possessiveness of this world to burn with her husband on the cremation pyre. ... Those who have such firm resoluteness are foremost. They never experience misery. Muktanand Swami says they are extremely happy.
In order to please God, I desire only to serve devotees of God in this life and all subsequent lives.
Only those who have accumulated a great number of merits from performing good deeds receive the opportunity to serve God’s Sant, but those who have a few merits do not.

When a person who wishes to worship God receives an opportunity to serve God and His devotees, he should serve them considering it to be his extremely great fortune. Moreover, he should do so only with bhakti for the sake of pleasing God and for his own liberation - not for the sake of receiving praise from others.
Remain as the servant of God. If you attain a low position, consider it your great fortune. Bhav (Shiva), Brahmā, and others certainly cannot find a place to sit near God.

By remembering God while performing activities, one remains at peace within. Seeing the peace within the devotee, the great Sadhu is pleased. And when the great Sadhu is pleased, one’s jiva becomes blissful.
My mind never becomes satiated with spiritual discourses, devotional songs, talks related to God or meditation of God. All of you should also do the same.

The means to transcend māyā is as follows: When the jiva comes into contact with the manifest form of Shri Purushottam Bhagwān - who is beyond māyā and who is the destroyer of māyā and all karmas - or the Sant who has attained that God, then by accepting their refuge, the jiva can transcend māyā.
Bhakti of God coupled with the knowledge of His greatness is the greatest and most steadfast means to eradicate one’s worldly desires.

If a person with shraddhā encounters the company of a true Sant and develops shraddhā in the words of that Sant, then all of the redemptive virtues of swadharma, vairāgya, gnān, bhakti, wisdom, etc., would develop in his heart, and the vicious natures of lust, anger, etc., would be burnt away.
Accepting the firm refuge of God is the single, greatest endeavor amongst all spiritual endeavors for pleasing God.

A devotee realizes, ‘This God and these sādhus all reside in Vaikunth, Golok and Brahmapur. ... Therefore, I am extremely fortunate in that I am able to stay in the presence of these sādhus.’ If he understands this, then he will experience awe all day and night and will sway in an ocean of bliss throughout the day.

I am extremely fortunate and completely fulfilled... As for me, the incarnate form of Purushottam has compassionately revealed His own form to me. ... Indeed, I swear by this assembly of sādhus that there is not even the slightest untruth in this matter. ... Indeed, I am very fortunate.’ Failing to think in this manner and failing to remain extremely elated throughout the day is a major deficiency.
That God and Sadhu we wanted to attain through endless austerities, chanting the name of God tens of millions of times, observances, donations and sacrifices, we have attained today.

This is an incredible opportunity and we have attained ultimate liberation. Today satsang is in the peak of its youth. We have received the central (soft and juicy) portion of the sugarcane. There is a lot of juice in it and is convenient to eat.

(1) Where is the jiva compared to Jagdish (God)? God is totally different (a different entity). ... (2) How can an ant ever hope to meet an elephant (kari)? It is impossible for them to meet. Similarly, there is a great difference between Purna Purushottam (who is extremely great and unreachable) and the jiva, which is imprisoned (by māyā).
I very much prefer one who offers bhakti with shraddhā and without jealousy.

If one abandons the desire for the fruits related to dharma, arth and kām, and if one performs pious karmas only to please God, then those pious karmas become a form of bhakti and aid in the attainment of liberation.
The only method for a person to please God is to serve devotees of God by thought, word and deed.

When a person who wishes to worship God receives an opportunity to serve God and His devotees, he should serve them considering it to be his extremely great fortune. Moreover, he should do so only with bhakti for the sake of pleasing God and for his own liberation - not for the sake of receiving praise from others.
We should please God, santo, we should please God. Then, all of our goals will be fulfilled. ... Nishkulanand Swami says we will attain the abode of God.
God is pleased with a devotee who becomes free of lust, anger, avarice, deceit, egotism, jealousy and matsar and then offers bhakti to God.

The best of all is that we have attained the association of this God and this Sadhu. There is nothing better than this and there is nothing better to understand than this. And what is the worst of all? That one attributes human traits to this Sadhu – there is nothing worse than this.

If one does not perceive faults in the great Sadhu but himself has faults, then God will worry about them for him. But if one perceives faults in the great Sadhu, then his sin becomes cast in iron and cannot be redeemed.

Just as the form of God in Akshardhām is resplendent with countless divine powers and divine light at the end of ātyantik-pralay, one should realize exactly the same regarding the manifest God in human form. One who realizes this is said to have known God perfectly.
My murti, my Dhām, my powers, and my muktas... All of these are divine. They [residing in Akshardham] are a spectacle to behold.

If he has intense shraddhā and extremely firm faith in the words of God and the Sant, then whatever type of tāmasik karmas he may have performed will be destroyed; the dharma of Kali-yug will also vanish, and the dharma of Satya-yug will prevail. Therefore, if one practices satsang with absolute sincerity, then no fault will remain in one’s heart, and one will become brahmarup in this very lifetime.
Bhāgwat dharma is upheld by maintaining profound love towards the Ekāntik Sant of God, who possesses the attributes of swadharma, gnān, vairāgya, and bhakti coupled with knowledge of God’s greatness.

Intense love for the Satpurush is the only means to realizing one’s ātmā; it is the only means to realizing the greatness of the Satpurush; and it is also the only means to having the direct realization of God.
Only one who follows the commands of the Satpurush is behaving as the ātmā.
All of the spiritual endeavors for attaining liberation are incorporated in keeping the company - by thought, word and deed - of a Sant who possesses the 30 attributes of a sādhu.

If a person develops conviction in the guru - who is the manifest form of God - in the same way that he has conviction in the non-manifest deities, then, as a result, he attains all of the arthas which are described as attainable.

A person imbibes the virtues of such a Purush, who has no affection for anything except God, by believing, ‘This Purush is extremely great. ... He also feels remorse after realizing his own flaws. While repenting in this way, vairāgya arises in his heart, and thereafter, he acquires virtues similar to those of that Satpurush.
The guru is the form of Bhagwan for one who serves the guru with a pure mind. ... Premanand Swami says, “Bhagwan himself remains present to attend to him.”
What is impossible to achieve with this human body? That which is practiced regularly can definitely be achieved.

From this day onwards, no one in our Satsang fellowship should utter such discouraging words. Instead, always speak courageously. Those who do speak such words should be known as impotent. In fact, on days when one speaks such discouraging words, one should observe a fast.
One should continuously engage in delivering and listening to talks on the glory of God and his Sadhu.

Maharaj has come here (to earth) with his Akshardham, pārshads and all his powers. He is exactly the same (today). He whom we wish to attain after death, we have attained during this life; there is nothing more left to attain. If this truth is not understood properly, the jiva remains weak. Once this is understood, the jiva will no longer consider itself weak and will acquire a different mettle.
The means to understanding this glory is profound association with such a holy Sadhu, and without it the true glory of God cannot be understood.
Describe the virtues of the devotees of God. By doing so, the jiva becomes brahmarup. And, in this, there is no effort.

Maharaj has delivered countless discourses for the moksha of the jiva. Of them, four are the life-force of the jiva. What are they? First, Maharaj’s upāsanā; second, Maharaj’s commands; third, attachment with the great God-realized Sadhu; and fourth, friendship with the devotees. These four principles are the life-force of the jiva and they should never be given up.
Devotees should maintain oneness with each other. The more one devotee becomes one and united towards another, the dearer he becomes to Me.

All devotees who worship God are divine. One who understands, accepts, and reflects upon this important message becomes immersed in divine joy and conquers the world. He remains constantly blissful and his joy never wanes.
The Bhakta of God is indeed nothing but a form of Brahma. That is why one should never perceive human traits in him.

I consider this assembly of satsangis to be far greater than the assemblies in Shwetdwip, Golok, Vaikunth and Badrikāshram; and I see all of these devotees as being extremely luminous. Indeed, I swear by this assembly of sādhus that there is not even the slightest untruth in this matter. Why do I have to swear in this manner? Because not everyone understands such divinity, nor can they see it; that is why I have to swear.

In no way should one abandon one’s loyalty to God and His Bhakta, even if while keeping that loyalty one’s reputation increases or decreases, or one is honored or insulted, or one lives or dies. In addition, one should not allow an aversion to develop towards them.
Obeying God’s commands and upāsanā are the two wings. Never let go of them. Then, one can easily go to Akshardham. Of that there is no doubt.
Only one who follows the commands of the Satpurush is behaving as the ātmā.
He who has affection for his beloved, God, will never disobey the wishes of his beloved. That is the characteristic of affection.
To do as the Sadhu says is best. To do as per one’s own wish is worst. ... To do as per the instructions of the Sadhu is without blemishes and to do as per one’s own desire is full of blemishes.
We should concentrate on following agnas. One agna from the Pragat Satpurush is far more important than a million other agnas
In His words lies withdrawal, In His words lies engagement; Through His words, all souls are freed — For every word from Shri Hari’s lips brings bliss and peace
Always introspect during every task and ask yourself, “I want to worship God, and what am I doing?” Keep thinking like this.

All of our satsangis should develop the following singular conviction: ‘We also wish to join the ranks of the aksharrup muktas and go to Akshardhām to forever remain in the service of God. We have no desire for the temporary and vain worldly pleasures; nor do we wish to be tempted by them in any way.’ Keeping such a firm conviction, one should offer ekāntik bhakti to God.

The earth remains stable and trembles; the stars remain steady in the sky; the rains fall; the sun rises and sets; the moon appears and disappears, waxes and wanes... these and a countless variety of other wonders are due only to the form of God that I have attained.’ With this understanding, he has the conviction that no one except the incarnate form of God is the cause of these wonders. He realizes, ‘The countless wonders which have occurred in the past, those which are currently taking place, and those which will occur in the future are all only due to the manifest form of God that I have attained.
At present we do not realize it, but we have attained God so we are fulfilled.
What can I say about the bliss, I cannot express it in words When I think of the bliss, my heart seems to burst

Today, waves of bliss surge within my heart — For I have attained the most precious treasure of all... In this divine ecstasy, Nishkulanand Swami sings with elation, Praising the Lord with heart full of wonder and bliss.

(1) Believe that our great fortune has awakened today. We have been redeemed countless times. ... (11) How blessed in this time, when we have met Maharaj. The bells of our victory are resounding today.

The jiva realizes, ‘My self is Brahma, which is transcendental and free from māyā.’ If one associates with Brahma through continuous contemplation in this manner, the jiva acquires the virtues of that Brahma.
One should develop oneness with one’s jivātmā and with that Brahma and worship Parabrahma while maintaining a master-servant relationship with Him.

One who does things with his body and offers devotion to God with the understanding that his true form is different from the body (i.e. ātmā) progresses a lot. But if he becomes one with his actions, that is not proper.
Whatever happiness exists in māyā is not without misery. This, too, should be kept in mind.

It (the jiva) does not indulge in the bliss of its own self; nor does it know its own nature. For this reason, it is the most ignorant of the ignorant, the most senseless of the senseless, the most foolish of fools and the vilest of the vile.

Since we have offered our body, mind and wealth to God, then now, only the will of God is our prārabdha; besides that, there is no other prārabdha for us. Therefore, regardless of whatever pain or pleasure we may encounter by the wish of God, we should not become disturbed in any way; we should be pleased with whatever pleases God.

If God seats us on an elephant, we should remain happy by sitting on an elephant; and if He seats us on a donkey, then we should remain happy by sitting on a donkey. Everything happens by the will of God. So, just as a dry leaf is blown in the air according to the direction of the wind, we should also remain dependent on Him and joyfully worship God, not allowing any frustration to enter our minds.

There are two means by which inner peace remains and no agitation arises: one is to worship God and the other is to understand God as the all-doer. Then, if we get happiness we should enjoy it and if we encounter misery we should tolerate it. It is said, “Dāsnā dushman Hari ke’di hoy nahi, jem karashe tem sukh ja thāshe.” – “God is not an enemy of the devotee, whatever he does will bring happiness.”

Maharaj, your māyā is extremely powerful. It has bound many men and women. Give us the boon that this māyā will not entangle us. ... This is the ‘fagwā’ that Maharaj gave his devotees. Who else is powerful enough to give such boons?
Learn to worship God from within. By doing this the desires for material pleasures will be reduced.

You also see this form of God, but you do not comprehend it fully. However, when you come to comprehend this fact, you will not encounter any difficulty in subduing the desires for the panchvishays and swabhāvs such as lust, anger, etc.; they will be subdued easily.
I do not wish to leave any trace of the world in the hearts of whosoever keeps My company.
That Akshar has two forms. One, which is formless and pure chaitanya, is known as Chidākāsh or Brahmamahol. In its other form, that Akshar remains in the service of Purushottam Nārāyan.
Some are controlled by the mind while some control the mind. This statement is worth contemplating on daily.
One who aspires for liberation should most certainly develop enmity towards his mind.
To do as the Sadhu says is best. To do as per one’s own wish is worst. ... To do as per the instructions of the Sadhu is without blemishes and to do as per one’s own desire is full of blemishes.
In Ingola, Shri Hari said: My devotees should not do as they please, they should remain in agna. Even if the one who does as they please follows many dharmas... he remains distant from me.
There is but one core truth in Satsang — To never disobey the divine command. The goal is to please the Lord alone, Yet let us not act in ways that earn His displeasure.
For a moment’s fleeting joy, One abandons the command of Shri Hari — But tell me, O brother, How can such a one ever attain eternal bliss?
Many speak of dharma, of righteousness and duty — Yet dharma holds profound secrets within. To live by the words of the manifest Lord — There is no greater dharma than this.
Once, Maharaj stood up and said, “Nobody should break the rules and those who want to, do not remain in the Satsang. Be good and do not stain this clean, pure and spotless blanket of character.
Never act against the sacred rules of conduct, Even if a fortune lies within your reach. Let not greed entice your heart, Knowing well — all gain from unrighteousness turns to dust.

When pleasure and pain both come together, Keep your mind steady and unmoved... But if you waver from your vow or faith, You will face the pain of worldly unrest. ... For what you have attained already, Is greater than Akshar.
Matrudeva Bhava, Pitrudeva Bhava A mother is like God A father is like God
Atithidevo bhava A guest is like God
I will definitely come to fetch my devotees at the end of their lives This is my promise to all of you, I wanted to let everyone know

Having become a devotee of God, if one commits sins and accumulates detrimental desires in Satsang itself while offering bhakti, then those sins become ingrained in one - as if etched in iron. Moreover, a graver sin than associating with others’ wives due to the influence of evil company is to look at a devotee of God lustfully while in Satsang. Female satsangi devotees are to be viewed as one’s own mother, sister or daughter. So, he who looks at devotees lustfully is a vile sinner and will never be released from that sin.
On seeing women, the men walk at a distance. They never pick up lost items belonging to someone else.

Whether he be a devotee of God or not, no meek person should even slightly be pained. Moreover, if one does hurt the meek, not only does one not benefit in any way, but one also incurs a sin equivalent to the sin of killing a Brāhmin.

If one abandons the desire for the fruits related to dharma, arth and kām, and if one performs pious karmas only to please God, then those pious karmas become a form of bhakti and aid in the attainment of liberation.
The wise must ponder before they act—To give alms to the unworthy Is to sow seeds upon barren ground. ... Devānand says — in the great royal court, The Lord repaid her with endless grace.

Realizing that Parabrahma, who is Purushottam Narayan, is distinct from Brahma and is the cause, supporter and inspirer of Brahma, one should identify one's jivātmā with Brahma and offer upāsanā to Parabrahma as a servant to a master.

One may engage in discourses, sing kirtans, and talk, but one does not believe 'I am not this body'. Therefore, one should constantly do bhajan thinking, 'I am not the body, but I am the ātmā residing in the body, I am brahma, I am akshar, and Paramātmā Parabrahma Purushottam continuously and manifestly resides within me.'

Our birth is for the purpose of achieving two things. One is to become aksharrūp, in which the body is an obstacle; and the second is to join with God, in which association is an obstacle in many ways. These two flaws should be removed.
I tell you one thing, believe it: we are the ātmā, not the body; believe your form to be chaitanya, the miserable body is distinct from it.
My only wish is to serve the devotees of God in birth after birth, simply to please God.
The opportunity to serve the Sant of God is attained by those with exceptional merits, but not by those with fewer merits.

When one who wishes to worship God gets the opportunity to serve God or His devotee, he should consider it his great fortune and serve them. He should serve them solely to please God and for his own liberation, out of devotion, but never for the sake of receiving praise from others.

Remain a servant of the merciful Lord... If you get to do menial service, consider it your great fortune. Even Brahmā and others do not get such an opportunity, but you have found a place at the feet of Purushottam.

If we perform activities while continuously doing bhajan, inner peace is maintained. Seeing this inner peace, the great Sadhu is pleased, and he whom the great Sadhu is pleased with becomes blissfully happy.
I am never satiated with the discourses, kirtans, talks of God, or meditating on God. All of you should also do the same.

If a devotee understands, 'This God and this Sant are the residents of Vaikunth, Golok and Brahmapur. And wherever that Sant and God reside, all those abodes are present; and the fact that I have attained the association of this Sant is my great fortune.' If one understands this, one remains constantly amazed and immersed in the ocean of bliss.

I am blessed and I am fulfilled; and the jivas in this world wander around troubled by lust, anger, greed, infatuation, arrogance, jealousy, hopes and cravings, burning day and night in the three-fold miseries. But the manifest Purushottam has compassionately made me realize his true form and freed me from all flaws like lust and anger, and kept me in the company of a Sant like Narad and Sanakadik; therefore, this is my great fortune. If one does not think like this and does not remain extremely joyful constantly, it is a great flaw.
That God and Sadhu whom we wanted to attain by performing millions of austerities, millions of chantings, millions of fasts, millions of donations, and millions of sacrifices, we have attained today.
We have gained an invaluable benefit and attained ultimate liberation. Today is the prime youth of Satsang and we have attained the middle part of the sugarcane. It has much juice and is also easy.

What comparison is there between the jiva and Jagdish? They are known to be distinctly different. Even if one gives away a hundred heads, it is something not easily attained... What comparison is an ant's gathering to this profound mystery? On one side is the perfect Purushottam Himself, and on the other, the jiva bound by many chains.

The greatest of all things is that we have attained the association of this God and Sadhu; there is nothing better than this and nothing better to understand. And what is the worst of the worst? It is to perceive human traits in this Sadhu; there is nothing worse than this.
One should not perceive faults in the great Sadhu. If there are any flaws, God will worry about them, but if one perceives faults in the great Sadhu, the sin incurred will be indestructible.

At the end of the final destruction, the form of God residing in Akshardham is full of infinite divine powers and light. One should understand the manifest human form of God to be exactly the same. By doing so, one has known God in principle.

Although God's form appears like a human, it is extremely divine. God has come exactly as He is in Akshardham. He does not have human traits like childhood, youth, or old age, nor does He pass away. The human traits that are visible are like the illusions of a magician.
My form, my realms, my divine enjoyments and my muktas; all are divine, you just need the proper understanding to see them.

If one has intense faith and firm conviction in the words of the Sant and God, then no matter how tamasi one's karmas may be, they are destroyed. One overcomes the dharma of Kaliyug and abides by the dharma of Satyayug. Therefore, if one practices Satsang with genuine devotion, no flaw will remain in their heart and they will become brahmarūp while still in the body.
Eat millet bread and worship God, there is nothing else to do. We should offer bread to God and to the Sadhu; they will surely give, give, and give.

Bhagwat dharma is nourished through the association of the Ekantik Sadhu of God, who offers devotion to God coupled with swadharma, gnān, vairāgya, and knowledge of God's greatness. Furthermore, the gateway to liberation for the jiva is also opened through the association of such a Sadhu.

If a person is as lustful as a dog, he becomes free of lust (if he associates with the great Purush); but if he superimposes the flaw of lust upon the great Purush, then no matter how lust-free he may be, he becomes highly lustful. And if he perceives the great Purush as angry or greedy, he himself becomes angry and greedy. But if he understands the great Purush to be totally devoid of lust, greed, taste, ego, and attachment, he himself becomes free of all these flaws and becomes a staunch devotee.

If there is a Sant possessing these thirty virtues, and one associates with him in thought, word, and deed, keeping the understanding of him as a guru and a deity, then these thirty attributes will also develop in the person associating with him. In this way, all scriptures state: 'When one serves the Sant, one becomes like the Sant.'

Intense love for the Satpurush is the only means to realizing one's ātmā, it is the only means to knowing the greatness of the Satpurush, and it is the only means to having the direct realization of God.
One who complies with the commands of the Satpurush behaves as the ātmā. As one continues to imbibe the virtues of the great Purush, one's devotion continues to increase.
If one maintains the association of a Sant possessing the thirty virtues in thought, word, and deed, then all the means for liberation are encompassed in his association.
If the jiva develops the same conviction in the manifest guru-form of Hari as it has in the non-manifest deities, it achieves all the goals that have been described to be achieved.

When a person who has no love for anything other than God sees that the great Purush is revered by millions, yet has not the slightest desire for worldly pleasures, he feels remorse. He says, 'I am extremely wretched for indulging in worldly pleasures and failing to understand the talks of God; shame on me.' Feeling such remorse, he imbibes the virtues of the great Purush and repents for his own flaws. By constantly feeling this remorse, detachment arises in his heart, and he eventually attains virtues like those of the Satpurush.
Wherever one finds the Naimisharanya field in the form of the Sant's association, one should desire liberation and remain there with a firm mind.
Just as the offspring is like the bull... so the disciple derives strength from the guru he attains.
What is there that cannot be achieved with the human body? Whatever one does with constant practice, it can be achieved.

From this day forward, no one in our satsang should say words devoid of courage; always speak with courage. One who speaks without courage should be considered impotent. And if such words devoid of courage are spoken on any day, one should fast on that day.
The jiva becomes like the words it hears. Therefore, if we listen to the words of a powerful devotee of God, the jiva gains strength, but associating with the impotent does not yield strength.

One should constantly talk and listen to the glory of God and His Sadhu. Maharaj has arrived here with His Akshardham, His attendants, and all His divine powers. They are exactly the same. Those whom we wish to attain after discarding the body, we have attained today while in the body; nothing is lacking. Because this is not understood, weakness remains in the jiva, but when it is understood, weakness is never felt in the jiva; the jiva becomes transformed. There is no other means as great as understanding this glory. Without understanding the glory, no matter how many other endeavors one does, the jiva does not gain strength. The means to understand such glory is the association of such God-realized devotees; without them, this glory cannot be understood.
One should speak of the virtues of God's devotees; from this the jiva becomes brahmarūp. And it requires no physical effort.

Maharaj has established countless types of talks for the liberation of the jiva; but among them, four talks are the lifeblood of the jiva. What are they? Firstly, the upāsanā of Maharaj; secondly, the commands of Maharaj; thirdly, affection for the great Ekantik Sadhu; and fourthly, a feeling of amity with the devotees. These four talks are the lifeblood of the jiva, they must never be abandoned.
Devotees should have mutual affection. The extent of amity one devotee has for another is the extent to which he is my very life.

All devotees worshipping God are divine. Whoever understands, firmly grasps, and contemplates the essence of this matter becomes engrossed in bliss and conquers the world. Their joy remains unbroken day and night.
The devotees of God are merely forms of brahma, one should not harbor human traits in them.

The assembly in Shvetdweep, Golok, Vaikunth, and Badrikashram... I consider this assembly of satsangis to be even greater than them all and I see every devotee shining with immense light. If I am exaggerating even slightly, I swear upon this assembly of Sants. Why must I swear? Because not everyone realizes this divinity, nor can they visibly see it, so I must take an oath.
Continuously introspect in all activities, asking 'I want to worship God, but what am I actually doing?' Keep analyzing this.

All of our satsangis should firmly resolve, 'We also wish to join the ranks of the aksharrūp muktas and go to Akshardham to forever remain in the service of God. But we do not desire the perishable and futile worldly pleasures, nor do we want to be occasionally lured by them.' Keeping such a firm resolve, one should constantly offer ekantik bhakti to God.

The jiva should understand, 'My true form is the brahma that is free from and beyond māyā.' If one constantly meditates in this way and Associates with brahma, the virtues of brahma are imbibed by the jiva.
Identifying one's jivātmā with brahma, one should offer upāsanā to Parabrahma as a servant to a master.

If one performs actions physically while maintaining the understanding that one's true form is distinct (as the ātmā) and does bhajan, it brings great fulfillment. But if one becomes the action itself and gets absorbed in it, it is not right.
Any worldly happiness that exists is not without misery. Keep this one fact in mind.

Learn to think with Sankhya. Without Sankhya, the five flaws—lust, anger, greed, taste, ego, and attachment—and the three types of miseries—adhyātma, adhibhūt, and adhidev—will not be eradicated. Without Sankhya, satsang is considered incomplete. Therefore, to remain happy, learn to think with Sankhya.

This body is made of bones; a woman's body is also made of bones, and a child's body is also made of bones. There is no substance in any of them. The lime is white dust, and this other is just ordinary dust. The body is dust, money is dust, relatives are dust, food is dust, houses are dust... but the jiva has attached itself to them, believing them to have value. But time will consume them all. Therefore, worship God; everything else is dust.

We are constantly aware of five things. One is the realization that we must definitely leave this body and die, and there is no delay seen in that; rather, it is our firm conviction that 'We are to die at this very hour, in this very moment.'

Since we have offered our body, mind, and wealth to God, then God's wish is our only destiny; apart from that, there is no other destiny. Therefore, whether happiness or misery comes according to God's wish, one should not become disturbed in any way. We should remain happy in whatever pleases God.

If God seats us on an elephant, we should be happy sitting on the elephant; and if He seats us on a donkey, we should be happy sitting on the donkey. Everything happens according to God's doing. Therefore, just as a dry leaf blows with the direction of the wind, we should remain submissive to God, joyfully worship Him, and not let any disturbance enter our minds.

One who neither enjoys the bliss of his own self nor knows his own form is the most ignorant among the ignorant, the most foolish among the foolish, the crazies among the crazy, and the lowest of the low.

There are two ways to keep the mind cool and from burning up: one is to worship God, and the second is to understand God as the all-doer. When happiness comes, enjoy it, and when misery comes, endure it. It is said, 'Hari is never an enemy to His servant; whatever He does will only bring happiness.'

Your māyā is immensely powerful; it has covered men and women. Please grant us this boon: May this māyā not influence us... May lust, anger, greed, evil intellect, and infatuation not corrupt our minds. Whatever obstructs us from worshipping You, we ask that it not bother us... Please do not place us away from You, O Lord. Do not give us worldly greatness, arrogance, jealousy, or envy... May we not be bewildered by Your māyā, may we not be bound by the body and its relations. May we never perceive faults in Your actions, and may we always understand You as flawless.

Even the greatest devotees of God have asked from God, 'Please protect us from māyā in the form of 'I' and 'mine', and grant us affection for You. And may we have the association of Sants who have crossed this māyā and have affection for You, and may we have love and affinity for those Sants.' Therefore, we should also do this, ask for this, and listen to, contemplate, and deeply meditate on this.
Learn to do bhajan internally; by doing this, attachment to the sense objects diminishes.
In the face of respect and insult, consider oneself as Akshar; no one is greater than us, so from whom should we feel respected or insulted?
What should one do when feeling bewildered? This question was asked. The answer given was, 'Chant Swaminarayan Swaminarayan... doing this bhajan resolves the bewilderment.'

You also see this form, but you do not comprehend it perfectly. When this matter is fully understood, there will be no effort required to conquer the five sense objects or traits like lust and anger; they will be conquered effortlessly.
Maharaj's resolve is to purify everyone. He does not want to let any impurities remain in the hearts of those who keep His association.
Therefore, keep the strength of Maharaj in your heart; there is no other way to eradicate offenses besides this.

There is no mantra more powerful today than the Swaminarayan mantra. With this mantra, even the poison of a black cobra will not affect you, the desires for the sense objects vanish, one becomes brahmarūp, and the bondage of time, karma, and māyā is broken. This mantra is extremely powerful. Therefore, chant it constantly.

references.source: Shāstrījī Mahārāje prasangopātt uchchārelā chār mahāvākyo:
references.text: Four great statements occasionally spoken by Shastriji Maharaj: (1) We are the bullocks of Aksharpurushottam. (2) Even if we have to sell ourselves for Aksharpurushottam, it is less. (3) If someone speaks the talks of Aksharpurushottam sitting on my head, it is still acceptable. (4) This head has been shaved for the sake of Aksharpurushottam.

The means to cross māyā is that when a jiva attains the manifest Purushottam Bhagwan, who is beyond māyā and the destroyer of all karmas and māyā, or attains the Sant who has met that God, then by their refuge, one transcends māyā.
Devotion to God coupled with the knowledge of His greatness is the greatest and unshakable means to eradicate desires.

If a faithful person attains the association of a true Sant and places faith in the words of that Sant, then all beneficial virtues like swadharma, detachment, discrimination, gnān, and bhakti manifest in his heart, and the impurities of lust and anger are burnt away.
The firm refuge in God is the single greatest means among all means; by it, God is pleased.
We extremely like the devotion that is performed with faith and without jealousy.

If one renounces the desire for the fruits of dharma, wealth (arth), and fulfillment of desires (kām), and instead performs those same auspicious karmas for the purpose of pleasing God, then those very auspicious karmas turn into devotion and are purely for liberation.
The means for the jiva to please God is to serve the devotees of God in thought, word, and deed.

When one who wishes to worship God gets the opportunity to serve God or His devotee, he should consider it his great fortune and serve them. He should serve them solely to please God and for his own liberation, out of devotion, but never for the sake of receiving praise from others.

Let us please Ghanshyam... Sants, let us please Ghanshyam; then all tasks will be accomplished. Know the wishes of Maharaj's mind and live similarly all day; if Jagdish does not like it, do not even ask its name. If hardships come in doing so, bear them with courage in the heart; remain perfectly unshaken and single-minded, then you will attain blissful rest. Look at the ways of the people of the past, they found peace after experiencing miseries; consider yourself dead from birth, never sitting idly in one place. These worldly connections are double-dealings today, abandon both price and place; Nishkulanand says, become fearless and attain the abode of Hari.

While taking the side of God's devotees, whether one's reputation increases or decreases, whether one gains respect or insult, or whether one lives or dies, one must never abandon the side of God and God's devotees, and never allow a negative thought to enter about them.
If someone takes the side of satsang just as strongly as they take the side of their bodily relatives, their foundation in satsang is unshakable.

If someone is beating a devotee of God or giving them trouble, and one intervenes to protect the devotee of God, even to the point of dying or getting injured, the scriptures declare: 'All of their five great sins, including Brahma-hatya, are eradicated;' such is the glory of taking the side of God's devotees.
Commands and upāsanā are two wings; they must never be abandoned. If observed, one will effortlessly reach Akshardham, there is no doubt about it.

Doing as the Sant says is superior, and acting according to one's own will is inferior. One who acts according to their own will, even if they have renounced heavily, single-handedly built an entire mandir, or brought countless people into satsang, is still lacking and will face obstacles someday. But if one only gets half a meal, is lazy, sleeps too much, and is filled with such flaws, yet abandons their own will and does what the Sant says, they are superior. Doing as the Sant says is nirgun (divine), and doing as one pleases is sagun (worldly).
One who complies with the commands of the Satpurush behaves as the ātmā.
One who has affection for God never disobeys God's commands. The mark of affection is to live in whatever way pleases God.
We should remain strictly firm on following commands. Following one command of the manifest form is greater than following millions of other commands.
By the Word one renounces, by the Word one engages; by the Word one is bound or liberated. Let us realize that all the words spoken by Shri Hari are the source of supreme joy.

One understands, 'The God I have attained is the doer of all these infinite wonders—by His support this earth remains stable, by His shaking it quakes, the stars remain suspended in the sky by Him, the rain pours because He makes it pour, the sun and moon rise and set by His command.' One must not believe anyone other than the manifest absolute God to be the doer of these wonders.

One who possesses faith combined with the knowledge of greatness understands: 'My liberation was accomplished the very day I had the darshan of God. Even the jiva who devoutly does my darshan or obeys my words attains liberation, so what doubt is there regarding my own liberation? I am already fulfilled, and whatever spiritual endeavors I do are merely to please God.' Know that such a person possesses faith combined with the knowledge of God's greatness.

If the supremely great Purush is pleased with someone, then no matter how impure their prior impressions may be, they are destroyed. If the great Purush is pleased, a beggar becomes a king; no matter how bad their destiny may be, it becomes auspicious; and whatever miseries are destined to fall upon them are eradicated.
We may not realize it right now, but we have attained God; therefore, we are completely fulfilled.

One on whom the great Purush is pleased constantly experiences joy within. The physical body may experience happiness or misery—there is no certainty about that—but as long as their faith continues to grow day by day, increasing every single day, one should know that 'the great Purush is pleased.'
Without the pleasure of the great Purush, the root seed of worldly desires is not eradicated.

Today there is joy in my heart... Today there is joy in my heart, I have found a supremely precious thing. Even by enduring millions of hardships, Hari is not found, but He has manifestly met me. Such immense joy... cannot be described in words; Nishkulanand sings His virtues with overwhelming exhilaration in this joy.
